dek: The iPhone Duo is here, Apple's first fold, seven years after Samsung's.

slides.label: What happened
slides.text: Apple just launched the *iPhone Duo*, its first folding phone, seven years after Samsung's Galaxy Fold.

slides.label: No Face ID
slides.text: The Duo skips *Face ID* completely and brings back Touch ID, likely because the fold leaves no room for Face ID hardware.

slides.label: Apps still catching up
slides.text: Many third-party apps aren't optimized yet. Slack, Instagram, DoorDash and WhatsApp already updated for the *new screens*.

slides.label: Hidden tricks
slides.text: Flip the phone to use the rear cameras for *selfies*, or lock two apps into an *app pair* for split-screen multitasking.

slides.label: Accessory issues
slides.text: MagSafe works, but wallets *stick out* past the shorter frame, and the phone tips over in magnetic car docks.

slides.label: Handle with care
slides.text: The inner screen's nano-texture finish can't be removed. A scratch costs $19 to fix, a full crack costs *$999* without AppleCare+.

slides.label: What's next
slides.text: Apple Pencil support and a new *Reachability* feature are both coming later this year via software update.

slides.label: Why it matters
slides.text: For indie iOS developers, especially *underrepresented* creators, being first to optimize for new hardware like this can mean getting seen first.

question: Would you pay $1,999 for this? Yes or no.

Apple's iPhone Duo is finally out, and it's the company's first folding phone, landing seven years after Samsung's Galaxy Fold. According to Wired, the $1,999 device skips Face ID for Touch ID, has app pairs for multitasking, lets you use the rear cameras for selfies, and comes with a fragile nano-texture inner screen that costs $999 to fix if it cracks.

Many third-party apps aren't fully optimized yet, though big names like Slack, Instagram, DoorDash, and WhatsApp have already updated. Apple Pencil support and a new Reachability feature are coming later this year.

For developers building for iOS, especially those from underrepresented communities, getting ahead on new hardware like this can be a real opportunity to stand out early.

caption_linkedin:
Apple's iPhone Duo, its first folding smartphone, is officially shipping, seven years after Samsung opened the foldable category with the Galaxy Fold. Wired's breakdown shows a device that's polished but still catching up in one key area: software.

Many third-party apps aren't optimized for the new 5.4-inch and 7.6-inch displays yet, even some that technically support it, like Instagram, still have broken UI elements. Apple's own apps look great; everyone else is playing catch-up.

That gap is an opening. Developers, especially those building lean teams without huge design resources, who move fast to optimize for new form factors tend to get noticed first by users and press alike.

The Duo also drops Face ID for Touch ID, likely a hardware tradeoff for thinness, and adds real multitasking tools like app pairs. Pricing starts at $1,999, with notable fragility risks on the inner screen.

Would you bet on foldables becoming the new standard? Yes or no.
